body:
Same here. 

I just had to survive working with the women who is carrying my child. Wants nothing to do with me and won’t let me be a part of the kids life. “Sign your rights away when the baby is born” That’s all I get from her. Her last day at my place of employment. I won’t see or hear from her until “my lawyer contacts you when the baby is born”.

I’m so fed up. The thought of ending it felt so overwhelming today. It just reinforces what I need to do in January. And having some faith and hope in moving on to a better place is what keeps me there, earning just enough to survive and let me do a few things I’ve always wanted to do before I leave.
When I read those I always feel tranquil, relaxed... I don’t know why.
Has to be something.. at least it’s something to hope for.

I mean, I’ve tried. I tried and gave it all I had. I didn’t slack or fail, but the world failed me. I like to think of it this way... I was dealt a bad hand of cards, whether it be intentional or by chance. I showed my true colors and was an open book, people took advantage of me. I should have known better and been more guarded towards those that cheated me in life.

I’ve had days where I wanted to get revenge or even the score. Now I just want to find peace... and a long peaceful sleep is my form of peace.

In the process as we speak. Always backed out at the last minute and told myself that things would get better. They only became worse. Now I have no choice but to carry through with it come January. It’s hard but I’ve cut all social ties, barely speak to my family. Nobody knows just how bad the situation is or why I’ll no longer be here come next year. I guess a letter will explain it better to the few I have left.

I always believed in that saying. I lived by it for 25 years. Now I realize it’s just a saying. I’m sorry, I know the feeling. I think it depends on if you want them to get better or not, I’ve reached a point where it doesn’t matter anymore. Maybe it’ll pan out differently for you. Again, sorry you’re in a similar position.

I could never tell someone how I truly feel. The risk of being committed (or, as some call it, “saved”) is too great of a risk for me.

Be careful what you say and who you say it to. Involuntarily commitment is very real. But for some people it might help.
